4
A student intends to measure accurately the diameter of a wire (known to be approximately
1 mm) and the internal diameter of a pipe (known to be approximately 2 cm).
What are the most appropriate instruments for the student to use to make these measurements?
wire
pipe
A
calipers
calipers
B
calipers
micrometer
C
micrometer
calipers
D
micrometer
micrometer

hints: Notice the two very different sizes given: wire diameter approximately $1\text{ mm}$ and pipe internal diameter approximately $2\text{ cm}$.
Compare the needed resolution: a $0.1\text{ mm}$ caliper uncertainty is about 10% of $1\text{ mm}$ but only about 0.5% of $20\text{ mm}$, while a micrometer reads to $0.01\text{ mm}$.
Think about access as well as size: which instrument has outside jaws for a thin wire and which has inside jaws that can open inside a pipe?
walkthrough: Identify the measurands: external diameter of a wire of about $1\text{ mm}$, and internal diameter of a pipe of about $2\text{ cm} = 20\text{ mm}$.

Recall instrument capabilities: a micrometer screw gauge typically measures up to $25\text{ mm}$ with resolution $0.01\text{ mm}$; vernier or digital calipers measure up to about $150\text{ mm}$ with resolution about $0.1\text{ mm}$ to $0.02\text{ mm}$ and have inside jaws.

For the wire, fractional uncertainty matters. With calipers, $0.1\text{ mm} / 1\text{ mm}$ is about 10%, but with a micrometer $0.01\text{ mm} / 1\text{ mm}$ is about 1%, so the micrometer is most appropriate.

For the pipe, the size $20\text{ mm}$ is within the range of calipers and the inside jaws fit inside the pipe. A micrometer anvil is for external measurement with small range and cannot measure an internal diameter.
Combine the choices: wire with micrometer and pipe with calipers. This is option C.

A.explanation: Calipers typically read to $0.1\text{ mm}$ or $0.02\text{ mm}$, so the percentage uncertainty on a $1\text{ mm}$ wire would be too large for an accurate measurement.

B.explanation: This reverses the instruments - calipers lack resolution for the $1\text{ mm}$ wire and a micrometer cannot reach inside a $2\text{ cm}$ pipe to measure internal diameter.

C.explanation: A micrometer reading to $0.01\text{ mm}$ gives small percentage uncertainty on the $1\text{ mm}$ wire, while calipers with inside jaws can span the $2\text{ cm}$ internal diameter of the pipe.

D.explanation: A micrometer is ideal for the wire but its small jaw opening and external anvil cannot measure the $2\text{ cm}$ internal diameter inside the pipe.
